citations.label: 1Password Off-by-1 Labs FLAWED study, headline clean-fix rate
citations.excerpt: Across six recently-disclosed CVEs, we produced 6,080 patches using two frontier, cyber-capable reasoning models. The average success rate for generating a patch that fully resolved the vulnerability (without materially changing application behavior) was just 26.0%

citations.label: 1Password Off-by-1 Labs FLAWED study, rate of patches that fail or add a vulnerability
citations.excerpt: Conversely, LLM-generated patches did not resolve the vulnerability, added a new vulnerability, or both, an average 53.9% of the time

citations.label: Trail of Bits review of the 1Password FLAWED study, the four design choices behind the headline
citations.excerpt: Our review of 1Password’s code and data found four choices that make its 26% clean-fix rate a misleading guide to ordinary patching work.

citations.label: Trail of Bits review of the 1Password FLAWED study, what the headline rate pools together
citations.excerpt: Its headline says models produced clean fixes only 26% of the time. That figure includes experiments that deliberately instructed agents to apply the wrong fix, along with experiments in which agents could not compile or test their patches.

citations.label: Trail of Bits review of the 1Password FLAWED study, share of trials given a wrong-fix instruction
citations.excerpt: Two prompts tell agents to apply the wrong fix. Those prompts account for 22% of the data.

citations.label: Trail of Bits review of the 1Password FLAWED study, share of trials that could not build or test
citations.excerpt: One evaluation mode prevents agents from building or running code and accounts for 36% of the data.

citations.label: Trail of Bits review of the 1Password FLAWED study, reanalysis of the testable trials
citations.excerpt: In those trials, 2,634 of 3,067 patches generated by 1Password’s models (86%) blocked the supplied exploit.

citations.label: Trail of Bits review of the 1Password FLAWED study, undisclosed standard error of the six-target mean
citations.excerpt: The six-target mean has a standard error of about nine percentage points, which the report does not disclose.

citations.label: Trail of Bits review of the 1Password FLAWED study, human first-fix failure rate from its own assessments
citations.excerpt: We reviewed the first fixes submitted for 2,265 vulnerabilities across 236 Trail of Bits security assessments from 2024 to 2026. The developers maintained the affected software, had detailed reports from our engineers, and knew we would review their patches. Even under those favorable conditions, 283 first fixes failed to fully resolve the reported issue: 12.5%, or one in eight.

citations.label: Trail of Bits review of the 1Password FLAWED study, confidence interval on the human first-fix rate
citations.excerpt: Accounting for multiple fixes from the same assessment, the 95% confidence interval is 10.5% to 14.5%

citations.label: Trail of Bits review of the 1Password FLAWED study, a human maintainer and an agent repeating one mistake
citations.excerpt: Two authors, one human and one agent, working separately, made the same mistake on the same bug.

citations.label: Trail of Bits review of the 1Password FLAWED study, agreement between model graders and human reviewers
citations.excerpt: Models grading their own patches matched human reviewers on the full five-category outcome in 65.9% of reviewed cases.

citations.label: Trail of Bits review of the 1Password FLAWED study, disagreement between the two model graders
citations.excerpt: The two models assigned different outcomes to 36.8% of the same patches.

citations.label: Trail of Bits review of the 1Password FLAWED study, a vulnerable upstream reference fix the grader missed
citations.excerpt: The authors found 248 generated patches that repeated an off-by-one error in the upstream fix. The automated grader caught that new vulnerability in only 24 of them.

citations.label: Trail of Bits review of the 1Password FLAWED study, maintainer acceptance of its own agent-written patches
citations.excerpt: Maintainers merged 126 of our 186 pull requests, an acceptance rate of 67.7%.

citations.label: Trail of Bits review of the 1Password FLAWED study, share of merged patches kept without a security revision
citations.excerpt: In 91 of those 126 pull requests (72.2%), maintainers accepted the security fix we originally proposed.

citations.label: Trail of Bits review of the 1Password FLAWED study, the follow-up audit of its own merged patches
citations.excerpt: We examined about 33,500 subsequent commits in Patch the Planet projects. When a later commit changed a file our patch had modified, we investigated whether it fixed a problem our patch had introduced.

citations.label: Trail of Bits review of the 1Password FLAWED study, what that audit found
citations.excerpt: The review found at least ten functional bugs; four build, test, or release automation bugs; and one performance bug. It found no exploitable security vulnerabilities.

citations.label: Trail of Bits review of the 1Password FLAWED study, what a comparison between agents and developers needs
citations.excerpt: Readers deciding whether to use agents need to know how their failures compare with those of human developers. Establishing which is more reliable requires measuring both under comparable conditions.
